what: Cadence makes the software chip designers use. Its tools lay out transistors, verify that a design works before it is manufactured, and simulate how the finished chip and system will behave. It also licenses ready-made design blocks.
customers: Semiconductor companies, cloud providers designing their own chips, and carmakers and aerospace firms designing electronics.
money: design, verification and layout software licensed on multi-year contracts
pre-built design blocks customers drop into their chips
simulation of circuit boards, packaging, airflow and multiphysics
moat: Only three companies can supply the full toolchain. Designs, scripts and engineers' expertise are built around its tools, and a chip project cannot change tools mid-stream.
risks: Export restrictions on sales to China have cut a meaningful market
A handful of large chipmakers account for much of revenue
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings
Semiconductor design budgets fall in a chip downturn
opportunities: Every AI chip programme, including custom silicon from cloud companies, needs its tools
Most revenue is recurring under multi-year licences, which makes it unusually predictable
Simulation software extends it beyond chips into whole systems
watch: Backlog and recurring revenue growth, plus any change in China export rules.
